title: CEO Interview with Francisco Almada Lobo of Critical Manufacturing
gist: Critical Manufacturing CEO Francisco Almada Lobo argues that factory-floor AI maturity is capped by execution maturity, so an MES that captures context at execution time is the foundation for AI. He sees advanced packaging as the fastest-growing demand area, with customers worried about ramp speed, packaging quality costs and stalled AI pilots.

themes.theme: Industrial AI Cliff and data context

insights.claim: Almada Lobo coins the Industrial AI Cliff: AI maturity on the factory floor is capped by execution maturity, so a factory that cannot say what happened to each unit cannot train or trust a model on that history.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Manufacturing AI value depends on execution-layer data capture, favoring MES vendors.
insights.quote: AI maturity on the factory floor is capped by execution maturity.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Manufacturers already have plenty of data but lack data carrying operational context such as lot, recipe version, exception and decision, which must be captured at execution time because reconstructing it from historians and logs is expensive and unreliable.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Context-rich canonical data models are the real moat for factory AI.

insights.claim: Many AI pilots stall when they meet factory data, while boards expect results.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pilot-to-production conversion in fabs is hampered by data foundations.
insights.quote: Boards expect results, and many pilots stall when they meet factory data.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: Critical Manufacturing has embedded AI copilots for natural-language queries and dashboards, and an enterprise data platform that structures equipment, system and site data into a canonical model for its own and customers' AI and agentic workloads.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: MES vendors are repositioning as AI data foundations.

insights.claim: Advanced packaging moves front-end complexity into the back-end through wafer- and panel-level processes, hybrid bonding and multi-node, multi-supplier die in one package, requiring die-level traceability through full genealogy; many factories still bridge separate front-end and back-end MES platforms with custom integration.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Packaging complexity creates demand for unified MES covering front-end and back-end.

insights.claim: Semiconductor back-end and advanced packaging is Critical Manufacturing's strongest and fastest-growing demand area, helped by its ownership by ASMPT since 2018.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Packaging is where software demand is growing most, per this vendor.
insights.locator: What application areas are your strongest?

insights.claim: When one package combines several high-value die a single defect scraps all of them, so customers need to know quickly and with certainty which units share an exposure and why.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Compound yield loss raises the value of genealogy and traceability software.
insights.locator: The second is the cost of quality

insights.claim: New capacity is being built in the US, Europe, India and Southeast Asia, often without deep pools of experienced operators, so systems must carry more process knowledge while people are still learning, making ramp speed a top customer concern.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Geographic fab diversification increases demand for knowledge-embedding automation.

insights.claim: The MES market has three groups: established front-end or back-end specialists, broad enterprise and automation vendors treating MES as one module, and newer data-first platforms that contextualize data but do not enforce how the process runs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Enforcement plus data is the differentiation argument versus data-first entrants.

insights.claim: Critical Manufacturing is preparing a SaaS offering for smaller and pre-volume fabs, and prefers to join greenfield projects early during facility design because MES decisions affect layout, equipment specs and staffing.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: SaaS opens the long tail of smaller fabs.
insights.locator: We are also extending the platform

insights.claim: Gartner named Critical Manufacturing a Leader in its MES Magic Quadrant in 2021, 2022 and 2023, and IDC placed it in Leaders of its 2024-2025 MES MarketScape.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Self-reported analyst recognition used as credibility.
